utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May I ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, and meanwhile we can hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask, do you have a gist what period of time you would need today?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I cannot give you the exact hours, but I'll try to make it as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. You're aware we are sitting until 12.30, and then from 2.00 to 4.30 today. And the same will be true hopefully on Monday, if it can be arranged by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please go for a moment in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Further questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before I give once again the floor to the Defence, after having reviewed the transcript of yesterday and the day before, there's one point that needs to be clarified. Without any hesitation and repeatedly, you testified on the meeting held the 7th of January, 1992, Orthodox Christmas in 1992. And in the beginning of the case, you testified that it was already at that point in time that you were elected for the position you after the takeover in fact took in the municipality of Prijedor. This was a question related to the Municipality of Prijedor only. And then yesterday, confronted by documents from first Banja Luka that the names have to be replaced and the word "Serbian" has to be added, and then on a document dating 16, 17 April, 1992, asked by Mr. Lukic, you said maybe I committed an error. And it was only then that I was elected. So there is this remaining discrepancy. I recall very well that when we discussed the establishment of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor, you mentioned that all this paperwork and, no doubt, it appears only later, it's only made public in the Official Gazette later. But in fact the Crisis Staff was established beforehand. Mr. Kuruzovic, because this is a very important question for our case, may I once again to ask you to try to do the very best and to answer to the best of your recollection what happened, in fact, during the meeting the 7th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have made a mistake. There must have been a discrepancy in my memory. Years have gone by, and you have to understand all these things happened a long time ago. On the 7th of January, 1992, there was the so-called founding assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor. It was the constitutional assembly, and I assume that all the people who would then be the Executive Board were elected. I believe that the president and the vice-president of the municipality were elected at that time and that others were elected later on, as I could see in the documents. So I must have been mistaken on the dates when things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, did all those persons later, as you say now, elected, did they participate already at that meeting the 7th of January, especially did Dr. Stakic participate in the meeting the 7th of January, and did he chair the meeting the 7th of January?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember whether Stakic was there, and I don't believe that all the others were there. As for Dr. Stakic, I assume that he attended that meeting. And when the municipality was set up, I don't know who was -- who opened that session of the assembly. And if Stakic was then elected as the president of the municipality, I believe that he took over the chairing of that meeting. And as far as I can remember, that session didn't last long, maybe an hour or an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And once again for clarification, where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was held in the amateur theatre downtown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And approximately how many persons participated in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly, but I believe there were more than 200 because it was attended by the representative of the Serbian people from the entire territory of Prijedor. I know that there were a total of 270 seats in the theatre. Now whether all the seats were taken, I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This was the constituting session, so it would be the first meeting of the Serbian Assembly. We learned yesterday on the basis of the document that that what happened in the middle of April 1992 was the fifth meeting of the Serbian Assembly. What now about the second, the third, and the fourth meeting of the Serbian Assembly? Did you attend these meetings as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember these meetings, and I don't remember having attended these meetings of the assembly. I know that for one period of time, I was a deputy in the Serbian Assembly of the Municipality of Prijedor, but I don't remember exactly when that was. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's continue, Mr. Lukic, please. Questioned by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll help you remember exactly the things that Judge Schomburg asked you about, so I would kindly ask the usher to show you Document S262.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English, the page number is 0302476.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For you, Mr. Kuruzovic, could you please open page on the bottom of which there is a seal bearing numbers 8605. These are the last four digits on that page. These are the minutes of the constituent session of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor. And it says here: "The session was opened by Prijedor SDS chairman, Simo Miskovic, who greeted all those present." He then read the opening speech. "The following agenda was then proposed and adopted." Under number 3 at the bottom of that page, it reads who the persons were elected, to what post at this founding session. "Election of the president, vice-president, and secretary of the assembly, and chairman of the Executive Board of the assembly." It continues: "The election and appointment commission withdrew to prepare recommendations of candidates for posts. The commission is composed of Dragan Savanovic, Dusan Kurnoga, and Ranko Radanovic. The SDS chairman Miskovic explained the method according to which positions not held by Serbs are filled." Again, it says, "Miskovic explained other organs are going to be established as well. At the commission's proposal, the following were elected. President of the assembly, Milomir Stakic, vice-president of the assembly, Dragan Savanovic, secretary of the assembly Dusko Baltic. President of the Executive Board, Milan Kovacevic. The closing speech was given by the newly elected president of the Prijedor Municipality Serbian People's Assembly, Milomir Stakic." Is this a summary of what happened at that founding session?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably it is. That's exactly what I understood in the question who chaired over that meeting, and that's what I said. And I said when the new president of the Municipal Assembly was elected, he thanked everybody, and he took over the chairing of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it also transpire from these minutes that this session of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor did not elect members of the Executive Board of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the end of the minutes after the closing word by the president, nobody said anything, so obviously this is the end of the session which took place on the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page bearing the last four digits 8607, that is the next page of this document. This is minutes from the fifth session of the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, and it reads that the session was held on the 16th of April, 1992. Under number 5, "nomination of the Executive Board members." Under (d), "election of the TO commander (municipal staff)." Does this refer to your election?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall no longer need this document for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The only question emanating from this document would be there's -- in the beginning of this document, if you could put it a little bit more to the top, there it reads: "The session was attended by 63 of 87 board members." When were these 87 board members elected, and had you been one of these board members? Directly on the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to 38607 where it says "the session was attended by 63 out of 87 deputies"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I don't know whether I attended the session. Most probably I did, but it was a long time ago. And others did not attend for various reasons. Some of them had military duty. Who were the others who did not attend, I don't know. This is not just an SDS session. There were representatives of other parties as well. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question was when were these 87 board members elected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The confirmation of the number of deputies took place on the 7th of January when the assembly was founded. I don't know whether everybody attended that founding assembly, but local communes sent their delegates, and they were supposed to attend the founding session. And I know how things are done. The first session has to make official the presence of the deputies and confirm their number. I believe that the total number of the deputies in the assembly should have been 87. Now whether they all a attended this particular session, I don't know. I can see here 24 of them were not present, that is, deputies in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Please, Mr. Lukic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the usher now to show the witness the Exhibit Number D6B, please. And also our 65 ter number -- actually, it's D48 now. D48, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kuruzovic, in front of you, you see two dispatches. One from the minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic, and the other sent by the commander Colonel Hasan Efendic from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Both dispatches were sent on the 24th of -- 29th of April, 1992. On the 29th of April, 1992, did you have the opportunity to see any of these two dispatches?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see them. But I heard about the contents of these dispatches. So on the 29th of April, around 1700, in the barracks where we had been invited to come, and I was told what the dispatch said. This is the first time that I see what is in it and to realise what it is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these dispatches the ones on the basis of which it was decided to take over the power in the Municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We won't be needing these exhibits any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like the usher to show the witness our 65 ter number 575, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kuruzovic, you have before you a document dated 17th of May, 1992. I think that at this point in time, we don't have the translation of this document, and therefore I'd like to ask you to read it out to us slowly so that the interpreters could interpret it, and then I will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the document please be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to read this document out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The command of the 343rd Motorised Brigade, printing number 36," I'm not quite sure, but I do see that it says the 17th of May, 1992, Prijedor. "Replenishment and joinder of combat units orders," as one can see, this order was submitted to the Territorial Defence staff of the Serb Municipality of Prijedor. "Pursuant to the order of the commander of the 5th Corps, reference number strictly confidential, 434-4, of the 12th of May, 1992, and conclusions adopted by the session of the Council for the People's Defence of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor held on the 15th of May, 1992, in relation to the provision of the singleness of command -- unity of command of all the units and the armed people loyal to the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I hereby order: "1, the commander -- the chief of staff of the Serb Municipality of Prijedor with the strict command and existing documentation will move to the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks and place himself under the command of the 343rd Motorised Brigade. The deadline, 18th of May, 1992, by 1400. "2, in relation to the further organisation, formation, and the performance of tasks of all the former formations, TO units established so far, volunteer units, and the armed Serb people, will be taken care of and regulated by the orders of the command of the region of Prijedor which shall encompass the senior officers of the above-mentioned units who will also be placed under their command. "3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be moved up. And could we have the whole page on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I have said: "3, all individuals, groups, units which pursuant to the above-indicated orders do not place themselves under this command will be considered as paramilitary individuals and units, and appropriate legal measures will be applied to them as envisaged by the orders of the Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "Commander, Colonel Vladimir Arsic." There's a seal here, too, of the garrison, and I can see that it says that it was signed "for," so I guess it was Radmilo Zeljaja, but I'm not sure because I don't recognise this signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D125. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as D125B. The English translation can be found on today's, the 28th of March, 2003, transcript, page 10, line 5 through page 11, line 11. And may I kindly ask you, Mr. Lukic, to disalert the translation unit that all the documents we have now in English, and they have been read out, that they don't continue translating.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll do so, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kuruzovic, is that the order that you talked about when you explained how the Territorial Defence, that is, your staff, was placed under the unity, under one command?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it does not apply only to us, but all the volunteer units, all the other units, everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this decision terminate your staff, the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was a military conscript, and this order is clearly the follow-up on the decisions of the presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I therefore had to act as ordered. After that, as a confirmation of that, that is what had to be done by the administration of the Municipal Assembly, in other words, I received a document relieving me of my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it wasn't only your staff, but also other units of the Territorial Defence which were resubordinated to the military command.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please explain, what is the difference between the manoeuvring and area units of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The manoeuvring units of the Territorial Defence are the ones which engage in combat operations, and the area units are those which were set up in the Prijedor Municipality, that is, in all neighbourhood community and all area staffs. So these are the TO units that are mentioned here, and they are not the Serb units but the TO units. That is all units which by the -- which the Council for National Defence had ordered to be mobilised in 1991. All of those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the 5th Kozara Brigade, was it a manoeuvring unit, in point of fact?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, as far as I know. These are the TO units. Those which were in the town, they were not a part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the manoeuvring units armed by the republic? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so, I suppose that the government took care of that, to supply them. But how, I wasn't really such a high-ranking officer to know that. But yes, that is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in contrast with that, are you aware that the area units were armed, supplied, and deployed by the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, municipality in the broader sense of the word. It was done by the command of that particular staff of Territorial Defence. And since the commander of that Territorial Defence was a member of the Executive Board, then everybody that had to be settled had to be settled through the Executive Board. In other words, the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will ask you something about the negotiations which preceded the outbreak of armed conflicts in the Municipality of Prijedor. Prior to the 22nd of May, 1992, that is, before the conflict at Hambarine, did you go to Hambarine to conduct some negotiations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, although I perhaps wouldn't call it negotiations. Those were talks between men, talks between heads of families. And I was taken along with the president of the SDA and the president of the neighbourhood community, and the imam, the religious official of the Muslim people there. I went there to talk with them, and I went with that gentleman, and they welcomed us and we talked nicely. Since problems had already started emerging in the town by that time and some had already started using arms without authorisation and stealing weapons from the staffs of the Territorial Defence, and it happened in Stari Grad so that those were the reasons why we went and tried to reach some understanding, that those people who were people of -- who were people of -- prominent people in Hambarine, that they should talk to them. Because these were younger people who were perhaps not fully aware of the consequences of such. And I remember that this was a very nice conversation, and they also shared our view that something was necessary -- something along those lines was necessary because that was the way to preserve the security -- to maintain the security and safety of their own people, and that is how we talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also talk in Puharska about these things?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Now, I forgot the name, but his last name is Kapetanovic, a prominent father of a family from Puharska, Puharska which is, as it is called in our language, an enclave, with a large number of Muslims living there, but there were a number of Serbs, and there was a TO unit stationed there. It was multiethnic unit, but had a much larger number of Muslims in it. And since they themselves, I mean they suggested that we talk about this, they were afraid there might be some excesses, and they asked that I go and visit them and I accepted it, not because I was chief or something, but because they knew me and I lived nearby and there were a number of my students there and friends. And we had a similar conversation as in Hambarine, and they promised and we promised that we would all do our best to maintain the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also have similar talks about this, how to calm the situation and bring the tension down in Cela?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In Cela once, and the second time, and I can't remember, some small problem let had cropped up. So a gentleman, I think his last name is Solo, he was a religious official, he came with SDA representatives and representatives of the neighbourhood community and said in the same vein that they are expressing their loyalty to the government, and that they would also do their best to maintain law and order there. And that they had heard that there were talks with other parts of the town and that they would do their -- everything within their power to avoid any excesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few days before the incident on Hambarine -- at Hambarine, did you also talk with people in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't do it in Kozarac. We did it in Prijedor. It was a largish group of people, also prominent representatives of the Muslim people. And we had this conversation for one - what shall I call it - official reason only. And there was no need for me to be present there because I had nothing to do, but they had asked for it because the school principal from there should have turned up. I don't know why. Perhaps because as a member of the SDA. There was an engineer, and a man who used to be the chief of police earlier on, and I believe he was a deputy in the former parliament of the -- in the parliament in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. I believe his last name was Sejmenovic. And we talked about how law and order should be ensured in Kozarac. And that members of the police which should have been, or rather, not should have been, but was part of the public security centre in Prijedor, that they should do their job. That is, to maintain the order, look after the safety of people in Kozarac, and a request was also made because the insignia had changed to put on the insignia that were at the time in use in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And it turned out that everything -- that nothing was a problem but those insignia. And I've remembered just now, since there was a large number of -- large group of people in the staff or in this Territorial Defence unit, in its staff, the possibility that somebody might abuse the weapons also existed, and also that some people who had nothing to do with the TO staff might come by weapons so that all of us together asked that weapons be seized from all the unauthorised persons and to keep those weapons in the police station in Kozarac to avoid -- to avoid that somebody who is not authorised do something stupid. And it was agreed, but they said that some people in Kozarac were not listening to them, that they were not heeding -- they would not accept it. And then we insisted, "right, if they refused to have those insignia, those patches, then let us have them at least say that they will perform their duty." I mean, those policemen not to do something else and not to say that this had to do something with the public security centre in Prijedor. And they said that they tried to talk to them, but they thought it wouldn't be of much avail. And I thought that the reputation that this man enjoyed would help to put it through, but you know how it all ended. And they would not allow people to go through the checkpoint, and there was gunfire on the 26th or I don't know. Some people, I guess, got killed, and the order came from the command, from the army command. I don't know whether that -- within 24 or 48 hours, that they should be disarmed, that this checkpoint be dismantled to allow the movement, but this was not complied with and after that the army responded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this meeting attended by Mr. Srdjo Srdic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know. I do not know who convened it, but it must have been either Mr. Srdjo or somebody from the public security centre, but I suppose they brought together eminent citizens so that we could talk naturally and to have people representing the Muslim people who could be trusted, hoping that an agreement would be reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting, was it agreed that people from the Kozarac police station, or rather the department of the police station in Kozarac would not be bound to wear those patches, but they should continue working?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said. When they realised that it would be difficult to reach an understanding, then we said, "right, they don't have to have those patches, but let us have them say that they will perform their duties and continue to cooperate, the public security centre in Prijedor," because that is how the chain of command prescribed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now mention the numbers of pages and lines that I will be referring to, but let it not confuse you because that will be only for Their Honours and for our learned friends, so that they can follow whether I'm correctly quoting the text that I'll be quoting. Page 6, line 18, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you if you accepted the results of the 1992 census. And you said: "Yes, since it was organised by the authorities, by official bodies." Mr. Kuruzovic, were you involved in the census of 1992 in any way?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the details about possible deficiencies, shortcomings and objections to the methods applied and the outcome of the census?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not officially, but like all the other citizens, I heard that - and I'm trying not to use any ugly words, any bad words - but I've heard that there were some tricks, that there were some machinations, that is, the Serb people in that town assessed, that is, considered, that is thought, that the number of the Muslim population was blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware in relation to the question on page 18 whether somebody who was not a member of the SDS could become a member of the Serb Assembly of the Municipality? You explained to us yesterday why you thought that Mr. Stakic had become the vice-president, that it was because of a large number of voters in Omarska. But are you aware that Dr. Stakic was a member of the People's Radical Party Veljko Guberina -- no, sorry, Nikola Pasic. The founder of the party is Veljko Guberina.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 21 refers to the attack on Hambarine, line 14 onward. You explained that it was a TO checkpoint. You are also aware that Aziz Aliskovic was at this checkpoint, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I spoke about that, I mentioned it. But I wasn't quite sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to override. Could you please be so kind and quote in context the entire sentence, because there's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 21, line 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, you mentioned one checkpoint. And the text, in fact, reads: "There were some checkpoints of the Territorial Defence." May I therefore ask you that part of the transcript you feel necessary to be read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namely, line 16. "In all these localities nearby, Hambarine and others, I won't mention others, there were checkpoints of the Territorial Defence. And the ethnic composition of the population determined the composition." And in relation to this, I wanted to ask you whether you are aware that Mr. Aziz Aliskovic was a professional policeman?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally, but later on, yes, I heard that he was a professional policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he wasn't a member of the TO? He wasn't a home guard? I mean, he was not supposed to be there at the checkpoint manned by the Territorial Defence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, except perhaps if he refused to obey and decided to stop working as a policeman and joined the Territorial Defence. But then they should have taken away his police uniform because it is then -- because it represents the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is for that reason that I'm asking you this: People who were passing by could have the impression that they were stopped by the police for regular police control.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and then they could trust that control, because the police was mostly respected because the police managed to protect peace and order in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 31, line 11, you say: "I did not consult anybody, nor did I ask for anybody's opinion. I simply let these people go from Trnopolje." And you are referring to the period when you decided that the conditions were no longer in place for you to keep people in Trnopolje. You continue: "And people from the International Red Cross told me that there was no reason whatsoever to feed these people here, and that they should return to their homes." I would like to ask you this: Up to that point, did the people from the International Committee of the Red Cross were of the position that there was a need to keep these people in Trnopolje and protect them there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say what they were thinking. I only know how they behaved. They were there in Trnopolje all the time. They paid us frequent visits, and they assisted us to help these people in Trnopolje in every possible way. And before the centre was dismantled, there were some 200 or 300 people there who didn't want to leave. They were waiting for the organised resettlement into other countries. But when these people said that there were no longer conditions for them to be there, and people thought that it was a promise and that this promise would not come through. And those who were from town, I asked them to go back to their families because a large number of people had already left and returned to their apartments in town. And those who still expected that they would be able to go abroad had remained. There were other people from other places. I don't know where from. And finally, they left, and the exit from Prijedor on the road towards Novi Grad, towards Bosanski Novi, I went to a house that belonged to my acquaintance, my friend, from the Muslim people, Suhad Kalender, and I asked him and his family and his neighbours to help these people, to give them accommodation before they made a final decision as to where they wanted to go. They wanted to go towards Zagreb, but in the meantime, I learned that at that checkpoint there were threats that they would be shot so I couldn't allow them to go. Fortunately, my friend Kalender, his family and some other families were of assistance, and they stopped those people for a while in their homes. I don't know what happened to those people later on, where they went and when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuruzovic, did you ever work in the municipal administrative bodies?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prijedor? No, never. I never did anything else but work in the school. I was a principal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you are not familiar with the structure of the administrative municipal bodies?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am old enough to know, but unfortunately I don't. And I was never in a position to ask for anything from the municipality. In my career as an educator, I did not have to go to the municipality, and I didn't have any contacts with the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you don't know what the authorities and competencies of the municipal administrative bodies are?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not officially. I just know them as a citizen. I know what they should be doing, but not officially and not to the tiniest detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what municipal body replaced the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What body preceded the Crisis Staff or what body replaced the Crisis Staff? I don't know what you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What body existed before the existence of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I am going to give you a wrong answer, but I believe it was the Municipal Assembly, which is a legislative body, and there was also the Executive Board, which implemented the decisions of the Municipal Assembly. When the threat of war, the imminent threat of war was proclaimed, I believe that the Municipal Assembly was replaced by the Crisis Staff. But this obviously was not a body which did not have a clue about what they were doing because its members were members of the Executive Board plus the president of the Municipal Assembly and the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly. So it was like a joint body consisting of representatives of the legislative authorities and the executive branch of the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now explain what the position of this Defence is, and I will use some documents to show you that you have misunderstood the date when the Crisis Staff started operating.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Honourable Judges asked you and showed you Document Number 180, so I would kindly ask the usher to show you these documents first. On page 1, under Number 18, we can see the decision on the establishment and organisation of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality. And it says that the Municipal Assembly of the Municipality of Prijedor at its session on the 20th of May, 1992, took this decision. I would like to ask you in this regard, could the Municipal Assembly coexist parallelly with the Crisis Staff, or are they mutually exclusive? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they were mutually exclusive. I don't think that they can coexist, and I believe I'm right in saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 16 May, 1992, there was a session of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, a ceremonial session, which was attended by Muslims and Croats, although not all of them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I attended that session, but I suppose that it may have taken place because it is the day of the liberation of Prijedor during the Second World War, and it was a bank holiday which was observed by everybody in town across the board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will keep this document for a while. Can I please ask the usher to show you Document Number S60 at the same time. This document was also shown by -- to you by the Honourable Judge Schomburg. This is the minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on 15 May, 1992. And we can see among the people who attended this meeting, your name is also here. The agenda under 1 reads: "Decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first conclusion reads: "The draft of the decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is approved." Therefore, on the 15th of May, you were at this meeting, and you discussed the draft or the proposition of the decision. So you discussed the draft decision or preliminary decision. Was it really a preliminary decision? We see that this was just a proposal, and the proposal was that a member -- a representative of the garrison should also be incorporated into the proposed composition of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, no arguments, it reads "conclusion."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude that before this date, the Crisis Staff did not exist? It certainly didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me based on this document? It is very clear. Maybe, in my head, I created my own confusion because I was appointed as the commander of the TO staff, and as such I attended meetings. But I can see now this was the Executive Board presided by Mico Kovacevic. But since it was a long time ago, I'm confused. I believe that at first it was the Crisis Staff, and it never occurred to me to give a second thought to the dates. But when the President of the Chamber asked me, I didn't talk to anybody. I didn't check any of the documents. I just checked the document that applies directly to me, and that was that decision. If I had gone through the documents, maybe I would have been given -- maybe I would have been able to give you better answers about the dates. But I just gave you my honest answers the way I saw things, and I apologise if I've made a mistake or I've -- or if I have confused you regarding the dates when things happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why I asked you whether you ever worked in administrative organs, the goal being to explain that you actually do not understand the functioning of administrative bodies and their organisation.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I quite agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which can be seen or which transpires from your answers given to the Honourable Chamber, and I'm going to quote them. And that's why I'm putting to you the position of our Defence, and I'm putting it to you that you have confused the sessions of the Executive Board and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to comment on this. I will no longer allow your arguments and at the same time putting answers to the witness. It is not for you to criticise the witness by telling that the witness would not understand the functioning of administrative bodies and their organisation and so on. Please, leave it for the Judges to come to an evaluation of the testimony of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 36, line 10, His Honour Schomburg asked you - I am going to read in English to avoid any discrepancy between what it says in the transcript and what I say - [In English] "How often would the Crisis Staff meet, as you said, two or three days after the takeover in the following period?" [Interpretation] Your answer to that question was, line 12: "Well, I thought that in the Municipal Assembly, I think there was a meeting of the executive committee every day, and at the same time, that was a Crisis Staff." [Interpretation] May we conclude, then, that you have confused these two bodies like you've said it yourself?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. It is obvious that I have made a mistake here and that since I never worked in such positions, I was a principal of the school, and these meetings were in the morning, they were very short. I attended them for a very short time and only seldom. I know that these meetings were chaired by the president of the Executive Board. But as I say, I got confused on things. I'm sorry. I apologise. All I had in mind all the time was the Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff, and always the Crisis Staff. So I never -- I never gave a second thought to any of the dates when things happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No need for you to apologise. I'm going to quote another question put to you by His Honour Judge Schomburg, page 37, line 8. [In English] "You testified that you participated only on limited occasions when you were present at a meeting of a Crisis Staff. Who chaired the Crisis Staff?" "The president of the Municipal Assembly, Dr. Milomir Stakic." "Who invited and where were these meetings held?" "As far as I know, there were no particular kinds of invitations. It was a sort of working meeting, so to speak. Colleagues would meet in the morning because that was the purpose of the executive committee. And meetings were held in the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor, in the building of the Municipal Assembly." [Interpretation] Was your confusion compounded by the fact that the meetings of these two bodies mostly took place in the same place?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 40, line 15, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you the following: [In English] "Page 38, line 18, you said today when asked about the Crisis Staff, it's a kind of daily work of this Executive Board. Would this mean that the Executive Board was -- could be equaled with the Crisis Staff?" "Well, technically, I think yes, except that alongside the members of the Executive Board, there were also the president of the municipality and the vice-president of the municipality." [Interpretation] Therefore, may we conclude that in this reply to the Honourable Judge, did you think that these two bodies were technically the same body?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on. You also mentioned on page 37 that the Crisis Staff got a different name and was renominated into the war presidency, and that 15 days -- that this happened 15 days after its foundation. Can the usher please show you Document S206 [Realtime transcript read in error "S26"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the transcript, it reads S26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, S206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuruzovic, you talked about a decision on the establishment of a war presidency some 10 or 15 days after the foundation of the Crisis Staff. We can see here that the decision on the formation of war presidencies in municipalities in times of war or the immediate threat of war was taken on the 31st of May, 1992, that is, 12 days after the foundation of the Crisis Staff which was established on the 20th of May, 1992. Is this what you had in mind when you gave your answer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously I made some disproportions in the dates because I had the impression that things developed really quickly. I had other things to do at the time. When I apologise, I apologized to the Chamber because it has turned out that I have created some sort of a confusion, but I should assume that these problems with the dates will not be -- but I don't want to interfere with what is the job of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rules do not allow for the Chamber witnesses to be prepared and go through the documents, unlike the Defence witnesses who are shown exhibits prior to their testifying, so we all understand you and all of us in the courtroom understand that Chamber witnesses are more uncertain about dates. Thank you very much. We shall no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Koumjian, you wanted to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I was just waiting for a question. It sounded like an argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. If you feel that's an appropriate time to take a break, then the trial stays adjourned now until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Lukic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need a witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course, when the witness is here. Only that you know about the plans for next week, it's not foreseeable when the testimony of this witness can be finalised. I don't believe that it will be possible today. Therefore, we'll sit on Monday, and also planned for Tuesday during the same sitting hours as of today. Immediately after the break, we have to come back to the question of a 65 ter (i) conference scheduled for Monday, 1.00. But please be prepared for this immediately after the break, this is at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kuruzovic, can we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 69, line 23, that is, it starts at line 20, His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you whether at the time the Serbs had intended to put in place one Serb state. And my question to you would be whether in 1991 and 1992, the SDS policy if, that is, you know it, was in fact to preserve the already existing state Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What scientists said is another matter, but as regards Republika Srpska, that is, Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the SDS policy was to preserve Yugoslavia, the state that had existed before. And as far as I know, the people in the referendum voted to stay in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, I'll have to correct you. I suppose you mean the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, put your questions in the form of a real question and not in the form of an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm in cross-examination. I can suggest the answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is not a cross-examination. It's a line of questions. The witness before us is a Chamber witness, please be aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read the question you put to the witness regarding this matter. "Isn't that true, sir, that at that point in time, the persons in office already aimed at forming a Serbian state, a one and only Serbian state?" So I think that I can at least put the questions in the same manner, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but then, please, in context, it reads in its entirety: Why does Mr. Kovacevic mention this connection, also not only Serbian Krajina, but also Serbia and Montenegro. Isn't it true, sir, that at that point in time, the persons in office already aimed at forming a Serbian state, a one and only Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that I can use "isn't that true, sir," in future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it true, sir, that other peoples, Muslims and Croats, at that time wanted to solve their national question?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina wanted a whole Bosnia-Herzegovina to stay in Yugoslavia and to keep their Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that the Serbs wanted to live in -- to share the state with Muslims in Sandzak, which is part of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't answer that question. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina ask that Sandzak be separated from Serbia so that they could live in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard anything like that, and I don't think they would want that. But that is my opinion. I haven't heard about it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you. Is it true that they wanted to live together with Muslims in Sandzak and by the very fact that they wanted to stay in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it goes without saying. If it says Yugoslavia, then all the people that live there, and if the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina wanted to live in Yugoslavia and together with Muslims and Croats in our country, and that presumed living with all the other peoples living in Yugoslavia regardless of the territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware whether the armed forces stationed in Sarajevo and Tuzla were much stronger than the armed forces stationed in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I do not know. I can make an assumption because both those towns are larger than Prijedor, and there were many barracks, and there were lots of troops there, in Sarajevo, and I suppose that would also go for Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will like the usher now to show the witness number S250, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please turn to page 12. These are documents of the 24th of July, 1992. XIX. I'm sorry, will you please turn to page 1. On page 73 of the transcript, line 11, this item was discussed. And as we have established, the decision of the Crisis Staff to relieve of duty the commander of the Serb Territorial Defence was handed to you two days later, that is, after the 20th of May, 1992, when this particular decision was taken. Going through Document S141 yesterday, we established that the Serb Territorial Defence was abolished on the 12th of May, 1992. Likewise, today we saw the order of the commander of the 43rd Brigade dated 17th of May, 1992 subordinating you, that is your staff, to the 43rd Brigade. Is it true, sir, that on the 29th of May, 1992, your staff of the Territorial Defence no longer existed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that the Crisis Staff, as at that time, it was standing in for the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, was due to notify you about this, that is, that you were being relieved of the duty of the commander of the Serb TO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was within their competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now turn to the page with decisions taken on the 5th of June. Page 77, line 4 says: "Order that the neighbourhood community agency in Cirkin Polje should vacate the premises of the former Crisis Staff." It is the former Crisis Staff that is mentioned here. Do you know which Crisis Staff is in question?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but I know that in large part of the territory, in many neighbourhood communities Crisis Staffs had been formed, and those had nothing to do with this one, with the municipal Crisis Staff. I believe it was set up earlier. I'm not quite sure, but I think it was in other neighbourhood communities, too, not in Cirkin Polje alone. I assume that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, will you please turn to decisions of the 10th of July, 1992, which is page 78, line 13. Item 2: "The conclusion that the regional command should secure the camp at Trnopolje." You said that you could not remember in line 18 of that decision -- that you could not remember the decision. Do you know if it was enforced?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this regard, therefore securing the camp at Trnopolje, was any military order ever issued in this regard? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I never received any orders in writing that would be referring to this conclusion. And on the basis of what I learned, I requested that they come -- that is, the platoons come every day, I mean platoons of the brigade. I wanted them to come every day and guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it then that every morning, the commander of the 43rd Brigade, or one of his officers, ordered to send a platoon or whatever unit to serve as guards in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, therefore, in relation to the security at the collection centre in Trnopolje, does it mean that the orders of military commanders were being executed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the order concerning the security, that is, guarding of this open centre of -- guarding people in that centre, that was obeyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I'd like you to turn page with conclusions of 12th of June, page 7 of the B/C/S version, and that is page 79 of the transcript, line 22. His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you in relation to item 2 about the decision concerning shorter working hours at the Kozarski Vjesnik in Prijedor. In relation to this, will you please look at another document which the usher will give you, that is, number 180, and turn to page 43. At the top of the page, we see number 31, and it's a decision of the Crisis Staff which under 1 says: "The work of all restaurants, coffee shops, and other catering facilities in the territory of the Municipality of Prijedor is prohibited." Then, I'd like you to turn to page 47 in the same document under 40, we have another decision of the Crisis Staff stated 10th of June, 1992, which under 1 and 2 says: "The earlier decision on the prohibition work of catering outlets is vacated, and the working hours are established. The working hours may be from 8.00 to 2000 hours." Under 2: "All food shops and stores which have the necessary working conditions can work from 8.00 to 1700 hours." "May work from 8.00 to 17.00." Mr. Kuruzovic, is it true that the Municipal Assembly in peacetime was responsible for laying down the working hours of public and private institutions?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it's done today, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you think that the Crisis Staff replacing the Municipal Assembly at the time was entitled to set down the working hours for Kozarski Vjesnik, even though it did not run the same?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, if Kozarski Vjesnik, as far as I know, was a shareholding society or a public company, but it was a shareholding company, and it was mostly privately owned, so whatever it applies to private grocers, why shouldn't it also apply to Kozarski Vjesnik? And since the Crisis Staff was replacing the Municipal Assembly, of course, they could take such a decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This same document, could you please turn to the decisions taken on the 17th of June. In B/C/S, this is page 8, the very bottom of that page under number 1.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the 16th here, not the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go to the bottom of the page, please. Under 1, this is an order on the establishment of a unified intervention platoon. I would kindly ask the usher to show you Document Number S79. Under 3 of this order, it reads: "The Crisis Staff shall give its consent to the members proposed for the platoon by the regional command and the public security station." Do you know whether this order was ever enforced, whether the Crisis Staff was ever given the opportunity to select people for this intervention platoon?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any such documents, especially in view of the fact that I was there very seldom. I was asked yesterday about this. I shared my opinion with you, and I told you that this may have been necessary. Now, whether it could have been done only by the military police and the civilian police in order to prevent the looting in the town and stealing of property, I believe that that was their job. But I don't know whether this intervention platoon really was ever established and whether it was really ever operational.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The intervention platoon of the public security station of Prijedor, did it have soldiers or only policemen on its strength? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I don't believe that there were any soldiers on the strength of that platoon because that would have been a totally different thing. The public security station is under the Ministry of the Interior, and the army is under the Ministry of Defence. So I don't think that there were any soldiers in that intervention platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there intervention platoons as parts of military units as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been the case, but I believe that those were platoons for special tasks in the military sense, but not in the town but on the front lines where combat was taking place. As for such things existing in the town, I never heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that there was either a police or a military or a mixed unit under the command of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I don't know why any such thing would be necessary in the first place, given the fact that there is the military and the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's go to the decisions taken on the 2nd of July, 1992. Page 10, the bottom of that page in the B/C/S version of the document.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me a minute to find this. I don't know what page I'm supposed to be looking at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 11, we're looking at number 7 there.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 2nd July and in the Official Gazette here I'm looking at pages 42, 43.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. We need the document number 250. Can you please turn to page 11, item number 7. This is a conclusion on the recruitment of the year or age group born in 1974. I would like to ask you this. The recruitment of this intake, was it carried out based on this conclusion or was it carried out based on legal provisions.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was providing for by the law and that this was carried out according to the law. But the times were rather strange, to put it that way and the Crisis Staff replacing the Municipal Assembly took the conclusion and in order for this to be carried out. But in our state whoever was of the military age had to be, had to go to the army and this was under the competency of the Ministry of Defence, so these people who were born -- these men who were born in 1974 were due to go to the army and this was something that was prescribed by the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page -- actually it is on the same page. We are looking at the next -- at enactments passed on 14 July 1992. Conclusion number -- it cannot be seen in the transcript, but in any case this is page 78, line 24, in connection with enactments taken on 12 July. So the conclusion on the prohibition on the individual release of persons from Omarska, Trnopolje and Keraterm. Did you ever receive this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw it. But there were individual releases of those people who wanted to go home or to Prijedor, and there were also organised transportations of people. I don't know whether people went home or not and why they did that, whether they left the centre because they didn't want to be there any longer or whether they joined an organised transport to go somewhere else. But in any case, I've never seen this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item number 8 of the same date, this is the conclusion on the appointment of the commission for the receipt of confiscated property and goods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could the usher please be so kind and provide this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 11 of this enactment --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me a minute, please. We're talking about the 2nd of June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, we're talking about the 2nd of July. We were already there. We're talking about page 11.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I can see 14 of July -- oh, well then, yes, I can see it now, 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The item above 14th of July, 1992, item number 8, "Conclusion concerning the formation of a commission to receive captured goods." You don't have to know the answer to my following question, and you can say so. But, Mr. Kuruzovic, do you know that under the prevailing regulation, the municipality is the owner of public assets and the abandoned moveable and immoveable property, and that was the case in the former Yugoslavia and that it is still the case in today's Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer need this document for the time being. Thank you. I would like to ask you something about the killings on Mount Vlasic. You've told us that you were asked by the command of the 43rd Brigade to write a written report about that event. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was on page 95 of the transcript, starting with line 13 onwards. This written report, did you give it to somebody else or only to the 43rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the 43rd Brigade. I believe the man in charge was Todic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now something about your membership in the Crisis Staff. Is it correct, Mr. Kuruzovic, that after the 29th of May, 1992, you were no longer a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Kuruzovic, that you occasionally attended sessions of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know to what extent, but I did whenever I needed to discuss the provisions of food and other things. But I would be there for a very short period of time. I would arrive before the session was called to order. I asked for assistance, and I would leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it then correct, sir, that after the 29th of May, 1992, you did not participate in the decisions taken by the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have now finished with my questions relative to Day 143 of this procedure, but I would like to ask you something about the things that were put to you yesterday, on the 144th day of this trial. Yesterday, we saw a document signed by Pero Curguz and yourself. This was Exhibit Number S12. His Honour Judge Schomburg asked you, why was it necessary for somebody to have a certificate issued by the Autonomous Region of Krajina if they wanted to leave the territory of Prijedor? I would like to ask you in this regard, Serbs who were leaving Republika Srpska, did they also have to have an approval from the Ministry of Defence allowing them to leave the territory Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, especially those who were of military age, who were conscripts. As far as I know, and this I based on the stories that I heard, that regardless of the ethnic -- their ethnic background, they all had to do the same thing. They had to pay their bills, they had to settle their debts towards the companies whose products they had used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to that, conscripts or able-bodied men, men fit for military service had to have an approval from the Ministry of Defence. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, otherwise they could not have been demobilised. The Ministry of Defence had to consult the army or the organisation where they served because all these things went through the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did one have to have a certificate or an approval even if one wanted to temporarily leave the territory, without being mobilised, for example, if one went on business to Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duration of the journey did not matter and did not make a difference. One had to have an approval from the Ministry of Defence regardless of whether the person was demobilised or whether they were leaving the area temporarily. I cannot be absolutely sure of that, but that is my assumption. I believe that that was the case, that everybody had to have an approval from the Ministry of Defence, which was obtained in consultation with the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the usher again to show you Document S180. Please turn to page 37 -- actually, turn to page 36 first. On the bottom of that page -- just a moment. Let's wait for the English version to be put on the ELMO. Under number 19, we can see the decision on the appointment of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality. And it says here: "The president, the vice-president, and members of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor will be the following persons or the following persons are appointed..." After that follows a list containing ten names and their positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher, please, to present the English version on the ELMO. It's page 36, I think. That should be correct. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the meeting of the Council for National Defence that was already discussed today, we saw that somebody proposed for a representative of the garrison to be appointed a member of the Crisis Staff. Does it transpire from this list that was adopted four days after that particular meeting that a representative of the garrison was indeed appointed a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't transpire from that list that he was appointed. He was not appointed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that the proposal put forth at the meeting of the National Defence Council which was held on the 15th of May, 1992, was not accepted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we leave this document, to the best of your recollection, following this decision dated the 20th of May, 1992, would it be correct in conjunction with your previous testimony that you had been only a member of the Crisis Staff for nine days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I can't tell you in days, but that may have been the case. Because the decision that I received on the 29th of May, the Territorial Defence was abolished, and I, as its commander, was no longer the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To the best of your own recollection as you sit here today, was it one week, two weeks, three weeks you were a member of the Crisis Staff? Because we still have some discrepancies in your testimony yesterday, the day before, and today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't remember what I said yesterday about the relevant dates. I was in contact with members of the Crisis Staff or the Executive Board whenever I needed something, but I would give them my verbal request when I had problems. But I didn't attend any official meetings. There was no need for me to attend any of those meetings because I stopped being a member of any of these bodies after the 29th of May when the Territorial Defence stopped existing. And that's when I got my decision that I was no longer its commander. I may have been confused on the dates, and I apologise about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour, for a break? Or we proceed until 12.30?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak more clearly and speak up, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interpretation service -- the interpreters are asking you to speak up if possible.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you were a member of the Crisis Staff for a short term only, could you tell us nevertheless whether it is true that the Crisis Staff could not issue -- could not adopt decisions to be executed by the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not think they could do it, except with regard to matters concerning life, that is, electricity, food, and so on and so forth. Things needed by the town, but otherwise directly, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware -- do you know if anyone ever was brought to military court, somebody who was a member of the army of Republika Srpska, because he had failed to obey the -- a decision of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me too much. I have no idea. I never heard anything like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I have to ask you about the police, too. Do you know, have you ever heard of anyone being brought to court whilst being a member of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska in the spring and summer of 1992 because he had failed to obey an order or carry out an order, decision, or whatever, of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would the usher be so kind and show the witness the Exhibit Number S60. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, you were asked about this, and you explained it, but I'll try to clear up some further things in this regard. This is the minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence. Item 5 of the agenda, taking over the duties of the military department. Mr. Kuruzovic, is it true that the military territorial body carried out the mobilisation in 1991 because the secretariat for the national defence had failed to comply with the law and did not mobilise people?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I know there were problems with assignment of people and the change of power. Whether it was all completed and where people went, I don't know. But I know there were some problems, and possibly something along these lines happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at this meeting of the Council for National Defence, there was discussion about the need of returning the mobilisation issues to a legal framework, or rather that the secretariat for national defence should once again be charged with these matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite sure that was that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe the witness said because he mumbled over the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness should be asked to repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interpretation service is not quite sure whether it heard you correctly. So could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was no doubt that a meeting must have discussed in this manner, to comply with laws and to mobilise the military conscripts regardless of which unit that that was the job for the secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that the Council for National Defence did not want to assume the responsibility for those matters? The Council for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Council for National Defence is not that kind of body. It is a kind of legislative body. And these are matters which are within the field of operation of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that the Council for National Defence had neither the staff nor the necessary equipment for that job?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KURUZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, let me ask you about something on page 17. Not that document, the transcript; I'm sorry.
